chunks: From him, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abdullah ibn Dhubyan, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'O Abdullah, there is no day of Eid for the Muslims, Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr, except that Allah renews grief for the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them) on it.' I said: 'And for what reason is that?' He said: 'Because they see their right in the hands of others.'

key_terms.فِطْرٍ: Eid al-Fitr (Festival of Breaking the Fast)

ai.seo_question: Why do the Imams feel grief on Islamic Eid days?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates that the grief of the Ahl al-Bayt is perpetually renewed on Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr because they witness their divinely appointed right to leadership (Imamah) remaining in the hands of others. This highlights the theological concept of 'Ghurbah' (alienation) and the enduring political and spiritual marginalization of the Imams despite the communal joy of the Ummah. The narration underscores that the festivals, while times of celebration for the masses, serve as poignant reminders of the delay in the establishment of the true Imam's authority.
